- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.

# Summary of 2015 UK General Election Manifesto

## Economic Policy

The manifesto commits to fiscal responsibility, pledging to reduce the deficit annually and achieve a budget surplus. All proposed policies are stated to be fully funded without additional borrowing. Revenue measures include restoring a 50p top income tax rate for earners above £150,000, abolishing non-domiciled tax status, and introducing a property tax on homes valued over £2 million. Business rates would be cut for smaller enterprises while maintaining competitive corporate tax rates.

## Employment and Wages

Key labour market proposals include raising the minimum wage to over £8 per hour by 2019, banning exploitative zero-hours contracts, and promoting the Living Wage through government procurement. A jobs guarantee would provide paid employment for long-term unemployed young people and adults.

## Education and Skills

The manifesto proposes reducing university tuition fees from £9,000 to £6,000 annually, guaranteeing apprenticeships for qualified school leavers, and protecting education budgets. Teaching standards would be raised through mandatory qualified teacher status, and class sizes for younger children would be capped at 30.

## Healthcare

Plans include recruiting 8,000 additional GPs, 20,000 nurses, and 3,000 midwives. Mental health would receive equal priority with physical health. The manifesto proposes integrating physical, mental, and social care services around individual patient needs, with guaranteed GP appointments within 48 hours.

## Housing

A target of 200,000 new homes annually by 2020 is proposed. Private renters would receive three-year tenancy guarantees with rent increase caps. First-time buyers would receive priority on new homes in growth areas.

## Immigration

Proposals include recruiting additional border staff, requiring a two-year residency period before benefit eligibility, and mandating English language proficiency for public-facing roles. Work rules would prevent wage undercutting through migrant worker exploitation.

## Constitutional Reform

Significant devolution of powers and £30 billion in funding to English cities and regions is proposed. Voting age would be lowered to 16. The second parliamentary chamber would be replaced with an elected regional senate. Further powers would be devolved to Scotland and Wales.

## International Affairs

The manifesto supports continued EU membership while seeking reforms, maintaining international development spending at 0.7% of national income, and conducting a strategic defence review. Climate change action features prominently, with targets for net-zero emissions and decarbonising electricity by 2030.
